item.title: India's Godrej Industries group signs pact to invest $2 billion in Haryana state
item.description: India's Godrej Industries group on Monday said it has signed a pact with the government of Haryana to invest 200 billion rupees ($2.09 billion) in the northern state, expanding its presence in the region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's Godrej Industries group on Monday said it has signed a pact with the government of Haryana to invest 200 billion rupees ($2.09 billion) in the northern state, expanding its presence in the region. The group has signed a memorandum of understanding with the state government with the investment expected to create around 40,000 jobs. Godrej Industries Group, which operates across consumer goods, real estate and financial services, has invested about 120 billion rupees in Haryana so far and employs around 9,000 people in the state. The group posted revenue of $7.2 billion in fiscal 2026. Godrej Properties (GODR.NS) , the group's real estate arm, will be a key driver of the investment and plans to deploy a further 160 billion rupees in Haryana by fiscal 2028, taking its total investment in the state to around 270 billion rupees. Godrej Ventures, the group's real estate private equity business, plans to invest another 35 billion rupees in office infrastructure in Gurugram. The proposed investment is expected to generate more than 30,000 direct and indirect jobs, it said. "Haryana has emerged as an important growth driver for the Godrej Industries Group," Chairperson Pirojsha Godrej said, adding that the group sees the region as a market where it can continue to invest for the long term. ($1 = 95.7250 Indian rupees)

item.title: EEUU cancela las maniobras marítimas con Corea del Sur ante restricciones por la guerra en Irán
item.description: Estados Unidos canceló un ejercicio conjunto de desembarco anfibio previsto para el próximo mes con Corea del Sur, según informó el lunes el Cuerpo de Marina de Seúl, después de que Washington alegara limitaciones en la disponibilidad de las fuerzas estadounidenses debido a la guerra en Irán.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Estados Unidos canceló un ejercicio conjunto de desembarco anfibio previsto para el próximo mes con Corea del Sur, según informó el lunes el Cuerpo de Marina de Seúl, después de que Washington alegara limitaciones en la disponibilidad de las fuerzas estadounidenses debido a la guerra en Irán. El Cuerpo de Marina de EEUU notificó formalmente a su homólogo surcoreano en junio que la disponibilidad de efectivos se vería limitada para el ejercicio a nivel de división, conocido como Ssangyong, según explicó un portavoz del Cuerpo de Marina de Corea del Sur en una rueda de prensa. Los aliados siguen manteniendo estrechas consultas sobre la reanudación de los ejercicios, señaló el portavoz. No especificó qué medidas podrían adoptarse para evitar futuras cancelaciones o para compensar las oportunidades de entrenamiento perdidas. Las Fuerzas de EEUU en Corea del Sur no respondieron de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. La cancelación se produce tras la orden sorpresa del presidente de EEUU, Donald Trump, de reducir la envergadura de otro ejercicio militar conjunto anual que finalizó el pasado viernes, alegando el costo y la negativa de Seúl a participar en la guerra en Irán. Trump también escribió en su plataforma Truth Social que los ejercicios "Ulchi Freedom Shield" enviaban "una señal totalmente inapropiada y hostil a un país que, desde que Donald J. Trump es presidente, se ha mostrado respetuoso y no ha representado ninguna amenaza". A pesar de la reducción de los ejercicios, Pionyang lanzó 10 misiles balísticos de corto alcance la semana pasada y emitió un comunicado en el que denunciaba los ejercicios. Corea del Norte lleva mucho tiempo condenando este tipo de maniobras conjuntas, calificándolas de ensayos para una invasión.

item.title: PSG coach warns players need to compete out of their comfort zone
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain players can ill afford to cruise through the season as coach Luis Enrique warned he expected them to play out of their comfort zone.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Paris Saint-Germain players can ill afford to cruise through the season as coach Luis Enrique warned he expected them to play out of their comfort zone. The PSG coach took off both Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at halftime of their opening game of the new Ligue 1 season, bringing on Mika Godts and Ferran Torres, who scored twice to [USN:L1N44K045 TEXT:"salvage a point at Stade Rennais"] on Sunday. "Football is like that. Paris Saint-Germain have won nothing, nothing," he said of the new season where they defend not only their Ligue 1 title but chase a third successive Champions League victory. "If you think about what you've won, you're not going to win anything! There is no credit. You have to show every day, every match, every training session, that you're ready. Otherwise, it's easy to relax and start slipping. "I wasn't brought up that way. We are always looking to win, and to keep winning, you have to step outside your comfort zone. Is that clear?" PSG, who [USN:L1N44915M TEXT:"won the European Super Cup"] this month but [USN:L1N44D050 TEXT:"lost the French version"] to Racing Lens, played a sluggish first half at Rennes and were 2-0 down at the break. But new Spanish signing Ferran Torres, who netted the winner in [USN:L6N43L077 TEXT:"last month's World Cup final"], came on for Dembélé and scored twice to ensure a point for the Parisians. "He wasn't bad, was he? He scored two goals, but I'm happy with everyone who came on in a very difficult match because we had a lot of trouble controlling Rennes in the first half," Luis Enrique said. "They were good on the counterattack and scored two wonderful goals. It was complicated, but it's important for me to see that so many players are ready. "We sign players to go on a long journey with them. It's very positive for him and we're very happy," he said of Ferran Torres' debut. "We're always looking to find the best players for every match. Places in the team will be more difficult to get than last year, and that's our ambition. "I think we had a very good transfer window, and we're still open to different possibilities. Everyone knows how difficult it is for a team to keep winning. And clearly, we still need to improve."

item.title: Posts distort El-Sayed’s 2022 remarks on Oklahoma Sharia Law proposal
item.description: A 2022 video of Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee in Michigan's 2026 U.S. Senate race, speaking about a 2010 Oklahoma referendum on Sharia law has been misrepresented online as showing him calling for the Islamic religious law to be implemented in the United States.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: A 2022 video of Abdul El-Sayed, the [USN:L1N4420RK TEXT:"Democratic nominee in Michigan's 2026 U.S. Senate race"], speaking about a 2010 Oklahoma referendum on Sharia law has been misrepresented online as showing him calling for the Islamic religious law to be implemented in the United States. Sharia is the body of [USN:L09475263 TEXT:"Islamic religious law"] based primarily on the Islamic holy book, the Koran, as well as the words and actions of the Prophet Mohammad. One X post said that El-Sayed “promotes imposing Sharia law on America” in the clip and that “Mainstream Muslims are trying to take over the U.S. government.” U.S. Senator Nancy Mace, a South Carolina Republican, also shared the video, saying it shows El-Sayed "clearly advocating for Sharia law in the U.S.” The clip comes from footage of an October 22, 2022, speech El-Sayed gave at an awards banquet for the Oklahoma chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR). During the event, El-Sayed criticized Oklahoma's 2010 State Question 755, a ballot proposal for a constitutional amendment that would have required state courts to rely only on state and federal law and prevent them from taking Islamic law into consideration in deciding cases. It is not unusual for U.S. courts to consider and even apply foreign or international law in cases involving cross-border disputes, according to the American Bar Association. Courts deciding international child custody cases, for example, apply the Hague Convention on International Child Abduction and may recognize foreign custody orders. A CAIR spokesperson [USN:TRE6AL5FK TEXT:"told Reuters"] in 2010 that the amendment, if it stands, risked nullifying legal contracts between Muslims. Oklahoma voters approved State Question 755 in 2010 with about 70% support, but it never took effect. Federal courts [USN:TRE80A00C TEXT:"blocked"] the measure after CAIR Oklahoma leader Muneer Awad sued, finding it likely violated constitutional protections by singling out Islam. The Oklahoma Election Board says the result was never certified due to the court order. El-Sayed made the comments in 2022 as part of a broader discussion of Oklahoma's history, saying the forces behind past injustices "are alive and well today." He then went on to urge Muslims in the state to stand for their civil liberties and rights, calling on them to be "witnesses for justice." At no point in the full video of the speech does El-Sayed call for Sharia law to be implemented in the U.S. El-Sayed’s campaign team declined to comment. VERDICT Misleading. The clip shows El-Sayed criticizing a proposed Oklahoma amendment, not advocating for Sharia law in the U.S. This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team.  Read more  about our fact-checking work.

item.title: California cancels talks with Paramount over Warner Bros merger, NYT reports
item.description: California's Attorney General Rob Bonta canceled a meeting with Paramount Skydance representatives scheduled for Monday to begin settlement talks over the state's lawsuit seeking to block Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery , the New York Times reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: California's Attorney General Rob Bonta canceled a meeting with Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) representatives scheduled for Monday to begin settlement talks over the state's lawsuit seeking to block Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD.O) , the New York Times reported. Citing a statement from Bonta's office, the newspaper said he accused Paramount of leaking details of a meeting held on Friday and acting in bad faith. Here are some details: “Not only did Paramount leak the alleged substance of settlement discussions, but they misrepresented these discussions, demonstrating a lack of good faith,” the report said, citing the statement. Paramount and the California Attorney General's office did not respond to Reuters requests for comment outside regular business hours. The New York Times [USN:L6N44J066 TEXT:"reported"] on Saturday talks between the two parties were preliminary, and there was no assurance that they will lead to meaningful negotiations toward a settlement. Last month, California and 11 states [USN:L6N43G09L TEXT:"sued"] to block Paramount's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, alleging the deal would lessen competition in film distribution and cable television, harming theaters and pay TV distributors. States including New York, Arizona and Minnesota argued the deal would harm theaters and television distributors, raise prices for consumers and make wages less competitive for workers. (This story has been refiled to correct spacing in paragraph 1.)

item.title: Moins de 20 navires ont emprunté le détroit d'Ormuz ce week-end - données
item.description: Le nombre de navires ayant traversé le détroit d'Ormuz au cours du week-end est resté très bas, à moins de 20, soit une fraction de ce qu'était le trafic avant la guerre entre l'Iran et les Etats-Unis, selon des données publiés lundi.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le nombre de navires ayant traversé le détroit d'Ormuz au cours du week-end est resté très bas, à moins de 20, soit une fraction de ce qu'était le trafic avant la guerre entre l'Iran et les Etats-Unis, selon des données publiés lundi. Quatre navires ont franchi le détroit dimanche, selon les premières données du service de suivi maritime Kpler et 13 samedi. Ces chiffres pourraient évoluer, certains navires ayant désactivé leurs transpondeurs lors de leur passage. Ce total état monté à 16 vendredi. Avant le déclenchement de la guerre contre l'Iran par les Etats-Unis et Israël le 28 février, entre 130 et 140 navires traversaient chaque jour le détroit d'Ormuz. En guise de représailles à cette guerre, l'Iran avait très vite fermé de facto cette voie essentielle au transport maritime mondiale d'hydrocarbures. Ceci s'était traduit par une flambée des cours du pétrole, qui restent à un niveau élevé, à plus de 90 dollars le baril, en raison de l'absence de tout progrès vers une résolution du conflit, les deux belligérants, qui clament tous deux contrôler le détroit d'Ormuz, brandissant au contraire la menace d'une escalade. Le volume global du trafic est resté faible au cours de la semaine s'achevant le 21 août, les navires ayant annulé leurs plans de transit ou modifié leur itinéraire pour passer par le nord du détroit à la suite d'attaques, note de son côté l'agence britannique Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) dans un rapport. Au total, 89 navires ont quitté le détroit tandis que 103 y sont entrés au cours de cette période de sept jours, selon ce rapport, qui s'appuie sur les données du système d'identification automatique (AIS). "Le trafic reste bien en deçà des niveaux normaux, les transits détectés par l'AIS étant inférieurs d'environ 90% aux niveaux de référence d'avant le conflit et en baisse depuis le pic enregistré du 24 au 26 juin", a-t-elle ajouté. Depuis le 6 juillet, l'UKMTO a signalé 23 incidents liés à des impacts de projectiles, ayant entraîné des dommages au niveau de la passerelle, de la salle des machines et de la structure de divers navires dans le détroit d'Ormuz et ses environs.

item.title: European shares slip as tech drags; Iran sanctions in focus
item.description: European shares edged lower on Monday, dragged down by technology stocks, while investors awaited details of threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran due later in the session.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: European shares edged lower on Monday, dragged down by technology stocks, while investors awaited details of threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran due later in the session. The pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) was down 0.1% at 653.40, as of 0713 GMT. The [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"U.S. threatened Iran"] with what it called "the greatest financial offensive ever marshalled" as it prepared to roll out economic sanctions targeting Iran's trade partners, while Iran vowed to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf "if the economic war continues." Energy shares (.SXEP) fell 0.4%, tracking Brent crude prices , which were at around $92 a barrel. On the upside, Basic Resources (.SXPP) was the top-performing sector, rising 0.8% as gold prices climbed on a weaker dollar. Meanwhile, the tech sector (.SX8P) was on edge ahead of Nvidia's (NVDA.O) results on Wednesday, as investors know how hard it will be for the chipmaker to meet stratospheric expectations. Market participants will also be hoping for clarity on the U.S. interest rate outlook when Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh speaks in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday, which will be watched for fresh clues.

item.title: BOURSE L'Europe ouvre en légère baisse, l'incertitude géopolitique pèse

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les principales Bourses européennes reculent légèrement lundi en début de séance, l'incertitude persistante concernant le Moyen-Orient et l'approche de la publication des résultats de Nvidia freinant l'appétit pour le risque À Paris, le CAC 40 (.FCHI) perd 0,20% à 8.467,56 points vers 07h14 GMT. À Francfort, le Dax (.GDAXI) recule de 0,26% et à Londres, le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) cède 0,05%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) perd 0,19%, le FTSEurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) 0,12% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) 0,13%. La semaine démarre sans grand enthousiasme pour les marchés d'actions, qui ne tirent pas parti de la baisse des cours du pétrole, l'incertitude liée aux négociations au Moyen-Orient pesant toujours sur le moral des investisseurs. Le nombre de navires ayant traversé le détroit d'Ormuz au cours du week-end est resté très bas, à moins de 20, soit une fraction de ce qu'était le trafic avant la guerre entre l'Iran et les Etats-Unis, selon [USN:L8N44L0C1 TEXT:"des données"] publiés lundi. De plus, les opérateurs attendent, plus tard dans la journée, des détails sur les nouvelles sanctions que Washington a promis d'imposer à l'Iran, ce qui pourrait encore compliquer les efforts diplomatiques et suscite une certaine attitude attentiste. À Paris, le secteur automobile cède du terrain, Stellantis perdant 2,80% et Renault (RENA.PA) 1,46%. Sur le plan sectoriel, la technologie (.SX8P) est également dans le rouge (-0,62%), l'approche des résultats de Nvidia, prévus mercredi, incitant le marché à la prudence.

item.title: PM Burnham says UK must be 'bolder' in seeking closer EU ties
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham told European Council President Antonio Costa that London should be bolder in pursuing closer ties with the European Union, with a UK-EU summit this year providing such opportunity, his office said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British Prime Minister [USN:L1N43M05W TEXT:"Andy Burnham"] told European Council President Antonio Costa that London should be bolder in pursuing closer ties with the European Union, with a UK-EU summit this year providing such opportunity, his office said on Monday. Burnham met Costa late on Sunday while travelling to Kyiv to [USN:L4N44K01O TEXT:"co-chair a meeting"] of the so-called "Coalition of the Willing" in his first visit to Ukraine since becoming prime minister. His office said Burnham told Costa that Britain should build on existing defence and security cooperation with European allies and seek closer collaboration across the relationship. The British leader told Costa that Britain "had to be bolder in terms of getting closer to the bloc", a Downing Street spokeswoman said of the two leaders' talks. "That included building on the close defence and security ties already forged between the UK and European allies to drive greater cooperation across all areas of the relationship." Britain has tried to improve its trading ties with the EU since it elected a Labour government in 2024, but progress has been slow, with frustrations emerging on both sides about what the former member should expect outside the main institutions. A spokeswoman for the British government said the two leaders agreed the UK-EU summit later this year would offer a good platform to continue that work. Burnham also met Luxembourg's prime minister, Luc Frieden, while travelling to Kyiv. They discussed different mechanisms for increasing defence spending, including the Canada-backed Defence, Security and Resilience Bank and the Multilateral Defence Mechanism launched by Britain, the Netherlands, Finland and Poland. Downing Street said the two leaders discussed how the two schemes could complement each other.

item.title: Iran warns vessels violating Hormuz transit rules of fines, detention
item.description: The warning heightens risks for charterers and shipowners.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iran has issued a warning that vessels violating its arrangements for transiting the Strait of Hormuz could face restrictions, including fines, detention, or confiscation, the Persian Gulf Strait Authority wrote in a post on X. The warning heightens risks for the charterers and shipowners whose vessels transit through the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for the world's energy shipments. The PGSA, a new body Iran has established with the aim of managing the strait, has said cargo owners should refer to an updated list of vessels deemed non-compliant for voyages relating to the Persian Gulf. Vessels engaging in operations including ship-to-ship transfers or transshipment with non-compliant vessels will also be added to the restricted list, it said. Ships seeking the removal of their names from the non-compliant vessels' list must submit a request with relevant explanations to Iran's maritime authorities, the post said.

item.title: "Salz in die Wunden": Chinas Netzgemeinde rechnet mit Professorin ab
item.description: Ob als Essenslieferant, Fahrer oder Paketzulieferer: Millionen Chinesen halten sich mit kleinen, meist schlecht bezahlten Aufträgen über Wasser. Mit der Bezeichnung dieser weit verbreiteten sogenannten Gig-Arbeit als eine Form von "Wohlfahrt" hat eine prominente Wirtschaftsprofessorin in China nun einen Sturm der Entrüstung ausgelöst.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ob als Essenslieferant, Fahrer oder Paketzulieferer: Millionen Chinesen halten sich mit kleinen, meist schlecht bezahlten Aufträgen über Wasser. Mit der Bezeichnung dieser weit verbreiteten sogenannten Gig-Arbeit als eine Form von "Wohlfahrt" hat eine prominente Wirtschaftsprofessorin in China nun einen Sturm der Entrüstung ausgelöst. Aus arbeitsökonomischer Sicht sei "Flexibilität an sich eine Form von Wohlfahrt", argumentierte Zhang Dandan, Professorin und Vizedekanin an der renommierten Peking-Universität, in einer populären Finanzsendung. Während Festangestellte ihre zeitliche Flexibilität gegen Rentenansprüche und andere Sozialleistungen eintauschten, genössen flexible Arbeitskräfte eine größere Kontrolle über ihre Zeit – allerdings auf Kosten einer schwächeren sozialen Absicherung. Die Kommentare zogen eine Welle der Empörung im Internet nach sich. Nutzer sozialer Medien warfen Zhang vor, die harte Realität der Gig-Ökonomie zu ignorieren. Zhang selbst reagierte nicht auf eine Anfrage der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters nach einer Stellungnahme. Die Äußerungen treffen in China einen wunden Punkt, da eine sich abkühlende Konjunktur feste Vollzeitstellen immer seltener werden lässt. Dem Forschungsinstitut China New Employment Forms zufolge wird die Zahl der flexibel Beschäftigten in diesem Jahr auf 320 Millionen steigen - das wären etwa 44 Prozent der städtischen Arbeitskräfte des Landes. Diese Zahl entspricht in etwa der gesamten Bevölkerung der USA. Branchenexperten warnen zudem, dass die Verbreitung von Jobs, bei denen Arbeitgeber keine Sozialversicherungsbeiträge leisten müssen, die ohnehin angespannten Sozial- und Rentensysteme Chinas langfristig zusätzlich gefährdet. Der einflussreiche Kommentator Hu Xijin, früherer Chefredakteur der staatlich unterstützten Zeitung "Global Times", nannte Zhangs Äußerungen "schockierend" und "inakzeptabel". Gleichwohl wiesen einige Nutzer darauf hin, dass sich Zhangs akademische Karriere bisher schwerpunktmäßig mit den Problemen von Gig-Arbeitern und der Forderung nach deren sozialer Absicherung befasst habe. Dennoch wurde ihre Bewertung von "Flexibilität" als Vorteil weithin als unsensibel empfunden. "Solche Kommentare von Experten sind nichts anderes als Salz in die Wunden derjenigen ohne Arbeitsplatzsicherheit zu streuen", schrieb ein Nutzer auf der Plattform Weibo. Ein anderer verwies auf den unerbittlichen Druck auf Essenslieferanten und Kuriere: "Jeden Tag kämpfen sie verbissen gegen den Algorithmus der Plattform, ohne Pause. Flexible Arbeit ist in Wahrheit keine freie Entscheidung, sondern eine unausweichliche Notwendigkeit."

item.title: El IBEX 35 abre plano pendiente de Nvidia, la geopolítica y Jackson Hole
item.description: El índice español IBEX 35 abría la sesión del lunes sin grandes variaciones, cerca de los 20.000 puntos, mientras los mercados aguardaban por los resultados de Nvidia el miércoles, en un contexto de altas expectativas en torno a la inteligencia artificial, y los anuncios de sanciones de Estados Unidos a Irán y sus socios comerciales, que se conocerán más tarde en la jornada.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El índice español IBEX 35 (.IBEX) abría la sesión del lunes sin grandes variaciones, cerca de los 20.000 puntos, mientras los mercados aguardaban por los resultados de Nvidia (NVDA.O) el miércoles, en un contexto de altas expectativas en torno a la inteligencia artificial, y los anuncios de sanciones de Estados Unidos a Irán y sus socios comerciales, que se conocerán más tarde en la jornada. Los datos del índice de precios del gasto en consumo personal (PCE, por sus siglas en inglés) de julio y el discurso del presidente de la Fed, Kevin Warsh, en el simposio de Jackson Hole de esta semana también serán objeto de atención en busca de nuevas pistas sobre las perspectivas de las tasas de interés en EEUU. "Toca esperar y ver. Sin susto, pero con cierta cautela. Es probable que las bolsas convencionales retrocedan c.-0,5%, mientras que la tecnología c.-1%. Después, estabilización hasta el miércoles noche/jueves por la mañana, según salga Nvidia", dijeron los analistas de Bankinter en su canal de Telegram. A las 0710 GMT del lunes, el selectivo bursátil español IBEX 35 subía 30,40 puntos, un 0,15%, hasta 19.991,90 puntos, mientras que el índice de grandes valores europeos FTSE Eurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) retrocedía un 0,12%. En el sector bancario, Santander (SAN.MC) subía un 0,18%, BBVA (BBVA.MC) se anotaba un 0,20%, Caixabank (CABK.MC) avanzaba un 0,27%, Sabadell (SABE.MC) ganaba un 0,60%, Bankinter (BKT.MC) se revalorizaba un 0,21% y Unicaja Banco (UNI.MC) subía un 0,17%. Entre los grandes valores no financieros, Telefónica (TEF.MC) se anotaba un 0,58%, Inditex (ITX.MC) avanzaba un 0,07%, Iberdrola (IBE.MC) se dejaba un 0,05%, Cellnex (CLNX.MC) ganaba un 0,96% y la petrolera Repsol (REP.MC) perdía un 0,57%.

item.title: Scentre to sell half of Queensland shopping centre for $632 mln
item.description: Scentre Group said on Monday Australian Retirement Trust will acquire a 50% stake in its Queensland shopping centre Westfield Mt Gravatt for A$882.5 million ($632.22 million), a 3.5% premium to the property's December 2025 book value.
item.dc:creator: Kumar Tanishk
item.content:encoded: Scentre Group (SCG.AX) said on Monday Australian Retirement Trust will acquire a 50% stake in its Queensland shopping centre Westfield Mt Gravatt for A$882.5 million ($632.22 million), a 3.5% premium to the property's December 2025 book value. Here are some other details: Over the past 13 months, Scentre has attracted A$3.1 billion in third-party capital by forming joint ventures around its assets under a long-term plan. The Queensland shopping centre attracted more than 17 million customer visits in the prior year and generated business partner sales exceeding A$1 billion, Scentre said. The group will retain management responsibilities. The deal includes the sale of a 50% direct property stake for A$870 million based on a 5.50% property yield and a 50% stake in adjacent land for A$12.5 million. Selling assets at sub-cost-of-capital yields is value-accretive, while retaining a 50% stake and full-property fee streams preserves meaningful exposure and unlocks capital for higher-value redeployment, said Emanuel Ajay Datt, MD of Datt Group. "We expect this transaction will firm up Scentre's ability to distribute income to shareholders," Datt said. The trust had [USN:L4N3XT06Y TEXT:"acquired"] a nearly 20% interest in Scentre’s flagship Westfield Sydney mall for A$864 million last year. Peer Vicinity (VCX.AX) , which owns centres including Queen Victoria Building in Sydney, has also been active in acquisitions. In May 2026, it [USN:TUEBWYJ0S TEXT:"purchased "]Eastern Creek Quarter in western Sydney from Frasers Property (FRPL.SI) for A$400 million. Scentre shares have traded in a range of A$3.28 to A$4.24 over the past year and have fallen more than 13% from their January peak. Its shares closed flat on the day. ($1 = 1.3959 Australian dollars)

item.title: Video appears to show 600 people abducted in Nigeria mosque attack, residents say
item.description: An armed group posted a video showing what residents said were about 600 women, children and older people abducted in an attack on a mosque in Nigeria’s north-central Niger State.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An armed group posted a video showing what residents said were about 600 women, children and older people abducted in [USN:L6N44J02S TEXT:"an attack"] on a mosque in Nigeria’s north-central Niger State. The video, posted on Sunday on Facebook and WhatsApp, showed large groups of people seated in a forested area surrounded by armed men. Several children could be heard crying in the background. Reuters could not independently verify the authenticity of the video. Police and state authorities did not respond to requests for comment. Mass kidnappings for ransom have become common in parts of northwestern and north-central Nigeria, where heavily armed gangs frequently raid villages, schools and highways. The video surfaced two days after gunmen attacked worshippers at the mosque in Dekara village during Friday prayers, taking people away in what residents said were simultaneous raids on several communities. Police had earlier confirmed an attack on worshippers in the area but said they could not verify the number of people abducted. In the video, a gunman speaking in Hausa addressed families of the captives and urged them to identify relatives among the people in the footage. "These are all your people. We are showing you this video so that you can identify your family members, your fathers, mothers, children and relatives," the gunman said. Resident Jamilu Ibrahim appealed to federal and state authorities to secure the release of the captives, citing the number of mothers with infants and children among those shown in the footage.

item.title: GSK scores regulatory wins for chronic hepatitis B drug, cancer therapy
item.description: GSK said on Monday its experimental chronic hepatitis B drug received its first global approval in Japan, and a key cancer therapy was granted a priority U.S. regulatory review as a possible rectal cancer treatment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: GSK (GSK.L) said on Monday its experimental chronic hepatitis B drug received its first global approval in Japan, and a key cancer therapy was granted a priority U.S. regulatory review as a possible rectal cancer treatment. Here are some details: The British drugmaker said bepirovirsen, to be branded as Hibsago, has been approved in Japan as the first and only functional cure for chronic hepatitis B in the country. GSK said the approval was based on late-stage studies, which showed that the drug helped nearly [USN:L4N4241LO TEXT:"one-in-five patients"] achieve a functional cure and raised hopes for a finite treatment course as an alternative to lifelong antiviral pills. Bepirovirsen is [USN:L4N4241LO TEXT:"designed"] to tackle hepatitis B in three ways: by blocking viral DNA replication, lowering hepatitis B surface antigen levels in the blood, and boosting immune response for longer-lasting control of the disease. GSK has predicted bepirovirsen could bring in over £2 billion ($2.73 billion) in peak annual sales, taking it closer to its annual revenue target of more than £40 billion by 2031 as its [USN:L6N43U0QG TEXT:"pipeline development comes into focus"]. Separately, GSK said the U.S. FDA will conduct a priority review of dostarlimab, marketed as Jemperli, as a potential treatment for a type of rectal cancer alongside existing approvals of specific endometrial cancer subtypes. The FDA has assigned a February 2027 action date for the rectal cancer review, with the program structure possibly yielding a decision earlier as well. Jemperli, which had also received both Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations by the FDA, is not currently approved anywhere in the world for locally advanced rectal cancer. ($1 = 0.7332 pounds)

item.title: Mercedes no longer have the fastest car in F1, says Antonelli
item.description: McLaren have taken a big step forward and Mercedes no longer have the quickest car in Formula One, championship leader Kimi Antonelli said after Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: McLaren have taken a big step forward and Mercedes no longer have the quickest car in Formula One, championship leader Kimi Antonelli said after Sunday's[USN:L6N44K04A TEXT:" Dutch Grand Prix"]. McLaren's reigning champion Lando Norris celebrated his second win in a row from [USN:L6N44J03J TEXT:"pole position"] at Zandvoort, with Antonelli and Mercedes teammate George Russell second and third ahead of Ferrari pair Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc. "We’re clearly not the fastest car anymore on the grid," said Antonelli, who won five races in a row earlier in the season. "We’re probably second or third, at least in today’s race, and McLaren has taken a huge step, especially since Hungary, since the big upgrade package they brought." Norris, who lost out to Antonelli at the race restart and then had to overtake him on track, questioned that assertion however. "I don’t think it’s true. I think if I didn’t get Kimi when I overtook him, I don’t think I would have won the race," he said. "For once I would give myself a little bit of credit that I feel like I’m doing a better job than everyone, and I think that can also make a difference. "We certainly have a car now capable of beating them ... but I think they have a better all-round performing car than what we do." Zandvoort, and [USN:L6N43S048 TEXT:"Budapest's Hungaroring"] before that, played to McLaren's strengths but some of the tracks coming up may be less favourable. Ferrari can be expected to go well at their home grand prix at Monza early next month, with upgrades in the pipeline, while Antonelli faces [USN:L1N44K03V TEXT:"hefty grid penalties"] for an engine change. A TOUGHER RIDE Mercedes are still way ahead of Ferrari and McLaren in the constructors' championship and scored more points (46 to McLaren's 43 and Ferrari's 31) than anyone else over the weekend. "We have a strong car in certain areas. It’s not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere," said Norris. "We’re very, very strong in high speed, and that’s the place we’ve improved the car the most, is high-speed performance. No one matches us in high speed, and that’s a good thing. "But the advantage that they (Mercedes) have to us in slow speed is also crazy. And therefore, I don’t have the confidence to say 'yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season. "I know I’ve just won two races in a row and had two poles in a row, but at the minute I don’t have the car I need to fight for a championship," added the Briton, who is 83 points behind Antonelli with another 11 rounds remaining unless the situation in the Middle East [USN:L6N43V0R3 TEXT:"forces a calendar change"]. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said cost-cap restrictions meant Mercedes did not have the money to put developments on the car as fast as they might like to. "We are trying to evenly split that through the season based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points," he told reporters. "So the ride has been a bit tougher than at the beginning of the year." McLaren principal Andrea Stella said he expected Mercedes to accelerate their car's development regardless. "I'm sure their car in the wind tunnel is quite a bit faster than the car they have on track," said the Italian. "And they will want to now convert some of this potential into upgrades that make it to the real car. I'm just pretty sure that they will have upgrades."

item.title: Volkswagen-Les salariés inquiets de la communication du directoire
item.description: Les salariés de Volkswagen ont critiqué ce qu’ils ont qualifié de "communication externe désastreuse" de la part du directoire, alors que le plus grand constructeur automobile européen envisage de nouvelles réductions de coûts, selon un article interne du comité d’entreprise consulté lundi par Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les salariés de Volkswagen (VOWG.DE) ont critiqué ce qu’ils ont qualifié de "communication externe désastreuse" de la part du directoire, alors que le plus grand constructeur automobile européen envisage de nouvelles réductions de coûts, selon un article interne du comité d’entreprise consulté lundi par Reuters. Un sondage en ligne, mené la semaine dernière par le comité d'entreprise du groupe, a révélé que les salariés et leurs familles se sentaient "inquiets et effrayés" par la communication publique de la direction, indique l'article. Les salariés ont également fait part de leurs craintes concernant la sécurité de l’emploi, l’avenir des programmes de préretraite et d’indemnités de départ, ainsi que les perspectives pour les usines de Volkswagen à Emden, Hanovre, Neckarsulm, Osnabrück et Zwickau. Dans une note interne diffusée vendredi, le président du directoire Oliver Blume a déclaré que quatre de ces usines ne devraient pas atteindre un taux d’utilisation des capacités compétitif dans les années 2030, mais a souligné qu’aucune décision n’avait encore été prise concernant la fermeture d’usines spécifiques. Les salariés ont critiqué le manque de précisions fournies vendredi concernant l’avenir de ces usines. Oliver Blume a rejeté les accusations selon lesquelles il dissimulerait des informations. "Nous tenons en permanence nos collègues et les représentants du personnel informés de l’état d’avancement des projets, par le biais de canaux internes, mais avant tout par le biais d’un dialogue personnel direct", avait-il déclaré en juillet dans un entretien publié sur le site web de l’entreprise. Volkswagen traverse actuellement ce qui est considéré comme la plus grande restructuration de son histoire, qui pourrait passer par 50.000 suppressions d'emplois supplémentaires et la scission de certaines divisions. Oliver Blume s’adressera aux salariés lors d’une réunion extraordinaire à Wolfsburg mardi, tandis que Thomas Schmall, directeur de la division Composants et membre du directoire, prendra la parole à Braunschweig. Le comité d'entreprise a convoqué ces réunions en juillet après que les représentants du personnel ont critiqué la communication de la direction concernant les plans visant à améliorer la compétitivité du constructeur automobile.

item.title: El ministro alemán Wadephul instará a Rubio a asumir un papel más activo en relación con Ucrania
item.description: El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores alemán, Johann Wadephul, tiene previsto hablar por teléfono este lunes con su homólogo estadounidense, Marco Rubio, para instarle a que se implique más personalmente en los esfuerzos diplomáticos relacionados con la guerra en Ucrania, según ha declarado a la emisora de radio Deutschlandfunk.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores alemán, Johann Wadephul, tiene previsto hablar por teléfono este lunes con su homólogo estadounidense, Marco Rubio, para instarle a que se implique más personalmente en los esfuerzos diplomáticos relacionados con la guerra en Ucrania, según ha declarado a la emisora de radio Deutschlandfunk. Wadephul, que ha estado recientemente en Ucrania, dijo a la emisora que, hasta ahora, la diplomacia estadounidense había recaído en gran medida en los enviados presidenciales Jared Kushner y Steve Witkoff. "Quizá yo mismo pueda animarle (a Rubio) a hacer más en ese sentido", dijo el ministro alemán, y añadió que Berlín estaba explorando otras vías para ayudar a reanudar las negociaciones. Alemania está en contacto con varios países, entre ellos Turquía, varios Estados del golfo Pérsico y Egipto, que mantienen vínculos más estrechos con Rusia que la mayoría de los países europeos, señaló Wadephul. Las negociaciones entre Rusia y Estados Unidos para poner fin al conflicto en Ucrania se han estancado en gran medida en medio de la guerra en Irán, y el Kremlin afirmó la semana pasada que aún no disponía de información sobre una posible próxima visita de Kushner y Witkoff. El viceministro de Asuntos Exteriores ruso, Serguéi Riabkov, había declarado el viernes en una entrevista que Rusia estaba dispuesta a escuchar las nuevas ideas de Rubio y a continuar el diálogo con Washington.

item.title: South African rand holds near multi-month high as Iran sanctions loom
item.description: The South African rand opened the week on a firm footing on Monday, hovering near its strongest level since the start of the Iran war, as a subdued dollar, higher gold prices and strength across emerging-market currencies supported the commodity-linked currency.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The South African rand opened the week on a firm footing on Monday, hovering near its strongest level since the start of the Iran war , as a subdued dollar, higher gold prices and strength across emerging-market currencies supported the commodity-linked currency. At 0636 GMT, the rand traded at 15.99 against the dollar , up about 0.2% and not far from its strongest level since the start of the Iran war touched earlier in the session. South Africa's key export, gold, hit its [USN:L1N44L03D TEXT:"highest level in more than three months"] as a subdued dollar lent support, while investors looked ahead to key U.S. inflation data and a speech by Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh later this week. The dollar was [USN:L1N44L061 TEXT:"pinned near multi-month lows"] as traders awaited details of a fresh U.S. sanctions package against Iran. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to hold a press conference at 1800 GMT after threatening "[USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"the toughest sanctions in history"]" on Iran, while Iran's foreign minister [USN:L6N44J01G TEXT:"dismissed"] the threat of new U.S. sanctions as a sign of desperation. Wichard Cilliers, head of market risk at TreasuryONE, said the rand's rally was being driven by broad dollar weakness, strong emerging-market sentiment and higher gold prices. Like other risk-sensitive currencies, the rand has been at the mercy of global market sentiment, particularly since the start of the U.S.-Iran war on February 28. South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond was slightly firmer in early deals, as the yield fell 1.5 basis points to 8.565%.

item.title: Thames Water's creditors line up new board under proposed rescue deal
item.description: Thames Water's senior creditors on Monday named the first group of proposed directors, including a turnaround specialist and a former civil servant, to oversee a decade-long overhaul of Britain's struggling utility if its rescue plan is approved.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thames Water's senior creditors on Monday named the first group of proposed directors, including a turnaround specialist and a former civil servant, to oversee a decade-long overhaul of Britain's struggling utility if its rescue plan is approved. Britain's largest water supplier, saddled with about £20 billion ($27 billion) in debt, has been fighting for survival after successive owners failed to invest adequately in its ageing infrastructure. The company has also faced public anger over sewage discharges into rivers. The senior creditor consortium, known as London & Valley Water, in July proposed a revised [USN:L4N43N0D6 TEXT:"rescue plan"] that includes a 10-year transformation programme and a possible 'golden share' for the government in an effort to avoid the company being taken into public ownership under Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government. The plan aims to invest in Thames Water’s infrastructure and address the root cause of critical issues such as pollution and leakage. The appointments hinge on the approval of the turnaround plan, water regulator Ofwat clearing each director, and a new capital structure being put in place through a court-sanctioned restructuring. The creditors, holding £17 billion of the troubled utility's debt, proposed installing broadband network Openreach's chair Mike McTighe, former Yorkshire Water CEO Liz Barber, ex-CEO of Openreach Clive Selley and former Permanent Secretary at the Department for Transport, Bernadette Kelly, to Thames Water's board. “It will take time to fix Thames Water, but we are committed to rebuilding trust with the customers and public Thames Water serves,” said McTighe, who would lead the governance overhaul and build the new Thames Water board. Collectively, the group of directors has experience in turning around businesses and running regulated utilities in Britain. “Thames Water continues to work constructively to reach an agreement that supports its long-term financial stability," a spokesperson for the utility said in an emailed statement to Reuters. ($1 = £0.7331)

item.content:encoded: La Comisión Europea aprobó el lunes una nueva ayuda financiera de 6.100 millones de euros (7.120 millones de dólares) para Ucrania, destinada a la adquisición de nuevos sistemas de defensa, como sistemas de defensa aérea, misiles, munición y radares. item.title: Report: 49ers trade RB Zamir White to Saints for LB Deion Jones
item.description: The New Orleans Saints are acquiring running back Zamir White from the San Francsico 49ers for linebacker Deion Jones, ESPN reported late Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New Orleans Saints are acquiring running back Zamir White from the San Francsico 49ers for linebacker Deion Jones, ESPN reported late Sunday. Both veteran players were free agents who signed earlier this month with their teams, only to be traded. The Saints could be looking for depth with five-time Pro Bowl running back Alvin Kamara expected to miss 4-6 weeks with a sprained MCL. New Orleans signed free agent Travis Etienne to a four-year contract worth $12 million per season but head coach Kellen Moore said he envisions using a deep committee of running backs. Jones would be reunited with the 49ers' new defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, his coach while both were with the Atlanta Falcons. White is listed on the 49ers "unofficial depth chart" on its website in the fourth running back group, behind starter Christian McCaffrey and four other players. White, who turns 27 on Sept. 18, played in six games last season for the Las Vegas Raiders and had 12 carries for 32 yards along with four receptions on six targets for 24 yards. Las Vegas selected White in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL Draft out of Georgia. For his career, he has 198 rushing attempts for 736 yards and two touchdowns and 25 receptions for 152 yards in 45 games (nine starts) for the Raiders since 2022. He became a free agent in March and signed with the 49ers on Aug. 12. Jones, 31, played in all 17 regular-season games for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last season as a reserve and totaled 29 tackles. He became a free agent in March and signed with the Saints on Aug. 7. Atlanta picked Jones in the second round of the 2016 draft out of LSU. He was third in the NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year that season when he intercepted three passes, returning two for scores. Jones made the Pro Bowl in his second year, when he made a career-high 138 tackles along with another three picks. For his career, Jones has 761 tackles, 12 sacks, 50 tackles for loss, 24 quarterback hits, 13 interceptions (five returned for TDs), 53 passes defended, five forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries in 128 games (91 starts) for the Falcons (2016-21), Cleveland Browns (2022), Carolina Panthers (2023) and Bucs (2024-25). Morris was a Falcons assistant coach (2015-19), defensive coordinator and interim head coach in 2020 and head coach again in 2024-25. --Field Level Media

item.title: India 419-6 at lunch after fifties by Pant, Jurel
item.description: Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel struck unbeaten fifties to push India to 419-6 at lunch on day two of the second and final test against Sri Lanka in Colombo on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel struck unbeaten fifties to push India to 419-6 at lunch on day two of the second and final test against Sri Lanka in Colombo on Monday. Pant, who had retired hurt on Sunday, came out to bat after the fall of debutant Saransh Jain. Pant's 63 not out included six fours and two sixes. Asitha Fernando (4-60) dismissed Jain (six), who was caught at slip. Jurel combined with Pant in a 112-run stand for the unbroken seventh wicket to pad India's score. Jurel hit five fours in his 59 not out. India are 1-0 ahead in the two-test series.

item.title: Equinor, Aker BP make gas find just northwest of Balder field
item.description: Norwegian oil firms Equinor and Aker BP have discovered gas in the so-called Linga prospect 10 miles northwest of the Balder field in the North Sea, the Norwegian offshore directorate said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Norwegian oil firms Equinor (EQNR.OL) and Aker BP (AKRBP.OL) have discovered gas in the so-called Linga prospect 10 miles northwest of the Balder field in the North Sea, the Norwegian offshore directorate said on Monday. Preliminary estimates put the size of the discovery at between 0.1 and 2.1 million standard cubic metres of recoverable oil equivalent, the offshore directorate said. Equinor operates the prospect and holds a 60% stake, while Aker BP owns the remaining 40%.

item.title: Report: Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty believed to have sprained ankle
item.description: Las Vegas running back Ashton Jeanty is believed to have sprained his ankle on Sunday during Raiders practice in Henderson, Nev., according to a co-report from ESPN and NFL Network late Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las Vegas running back Ashton Jeanty is believed to have sprained his ankle on Sunday during Raiders practice in Henderson, Nev., according to a co-report from ESPN and NFL Network late Sunday. Jeanty dove for an attempted reception on a pass route and fell awkwardly on the indoor turf surface, per multiple reports. Jeanty stayed down before being helped from the field by trainers and medical personnel. Jeanty couldn't put weight on his right leg as he left the scene. Raiders players knelt and prayed as Jeanty was assisted. The team declined comment on Jeanty's status, though it's not considered a long-term injury, per the report. Jeanty, 22, is entering his second season after the Raiders made him the No. 6 overall pick in last year's draft. He has been expected to be a major contributor for the Raiders this season. As a rookie, Jeanty ran for 975 yards with five touchdowns. He added 55 receptions for 346 yards and five touchdowns through the air. If Jeanty's injury is serious, it could mean a larger role for rookie Mike Washington Jr., who has been a star of training camp and was a fourth-round choice of the Raiders this spring. --Field Level Media

item.title: Volkswagen workers criticise board's communication
item.description: Volkswagen employees have criticised what they called the management board's "disastrous external communication" as Europe's largest automaker considers further cost cuts.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Volkswagen (VOWG.DE) employees have criticised what they called the management board's "disastrous external communication" as Europe's largest automaker considers [USN:L8N44I0TG TEXT:"further cost cuts"], according to an internal works council article seen by Reuters on Monday. An online survey, conducted last week by Volkswagen's Group works council, found that employees and their families were "unsettled and frightened" by the board's public communication, the article said. Employees also raised concerns about job security, the future of early-retirement and severance programmes, and prospects for Volkswagen's plants in Emden, Hanover, Neckarsulm, Osnabrueck and Zwickau. In [USN:L8N44I0TG TEXT:"an internal company memo on Friday"], CEO Oliver Blume said four of those plants were not expected to reach competitive capacity utilisation in the 2030s, but stressed that there was no decision yet on specific plant closures. The workers criticised the lack of details on the future of these plants provided on Friday. Blume has rejected accusations of withholding information. "We continuously keep our colleagues and employee representatives informed about the status of the plans—through internal channels, but above all through direct personal dialogue," he said in July in an interview published on the company's website. Volkswagen is undergoing what is considered to be its largest-ever restructuring, possibly ranging from a further [USN:L8N42Y0CC TEXT:"50,000 job cuts"] to the [USN:L8N42Y1AR TEXT:"carve-out of some divisions"]. Blume will address employees at an extraordinary meeting in Wolfsburg on Tuesday and Thomas Schmall, head of components and a member of the management board, will speak in Braunschweig. The works council called the meetings in July after employee representatives criticised the management's communication over plans to improve the automaker's competitiveness.

item.title: Taiwan indicts nine over alleged illegal export of AI servers to China
item.description: Taiwan prosecutors said on Monday they indicted nine people, including employees of Nvidia and Super Micro , accused of illegal export of artificial intelligence servers to China.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Taiwan prosecutors said on Monday they indicted nine people, including employees of Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Super Micro (SMCI.O) , accused of illegal export of artificial intelligence servers to China. Semiconductor powerhouse Taiwan is the world's largest producer of advanced chips used in AI applications. Prosecutors this year investigated the suspected illegal export of servers equipped with Nvidia chips subject to U.S. export controls. Washington has imposed curbs since 2022 making it illegal for such semiconductors to be exported or sold in China. In a statement, the prosecutors in the northern port city of Keelung said the defendants, whose full names they did not state, were "fully aware" that both Nvidia and Super Micro have "rigorous internal control procedures" regarding exports. However, the defendants "colluded with one another at various levels for enormous profit, illegally exporting high-end servers, increasing corporate compliance costs, and severely damaging our nation's international image", they added. Neither Nvidia nor Super Micro immediately responded to requests for comment. Taiwan has tightened export controls in recent years to keep advanced technology and know-how from reaching China, which claims the democratically governed island as its own territory despite the strong objections of the island's government.

item.title: Xiaomi launches new Xring chip, partners with TSMC for production, sources say
item.description: Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi on Monday unveiled a new version of its in-house Xring handset processor, betting that deeper control over key components will help strengthen its supply chain and reduce reliance on external chip suppliers.
item.dc:creator: Che Pan, Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi (1810.HK) on Monday unveiled a new version of its in-house Xring handset processor, betting that deeper control over key components will help strengthen its supply chain and reduce reliance on external chip suppliers. The introduction of Xring O3 comes a year after Xiaomi launched its first proprietary smartphone processor, the Xring O1, marking the latest step in the world's third-largest smartphone vendor's push to join rivals such as Apple (AAPL.O) , Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and Huawei in developing its own chips. TSMC (2330.TW) will manufacture the new chip using its 3-nanometre production technology, two people familiar with the matter said. One of the sources said the chip is expected to power Xiaomi's upcoming flagship folding phone, with a shipment target of 200,000 to 300,000 units. Xiaomi's expansion into foldable phones, a more expensive segment of the market, could challenge leading domestic player Huawei. Huawei shipped 1.6 million foldable phones in China in the second quarter, giving it a 68% market share, followed by Honor with 13.7% and Oppo with 8.5%, according to research firm Smart Analytics Global. The people declined to be identified because the plans are not public. Xiaomi and TSMC did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the chip's manufacturer, production technology or shipment targets. Smartphone processors, or system-on-chips (SoC), integrate computing, graphics, AI processing and imaging functions into a single component. DEVICE MAKERS PUSH FOR IN-HOUSE CHIPS Xiaomi's chip push reflects a broader industry trend as device makers seek to differentiate products and lessen dependence on suppliers such as Qualcomm (QCOM.O) and MediaTek (2454.TW) amid intensifying competition in premium smartphones. Xiaomi said during an earnings call last week that cumulative shipments of devices powered by the Xring O1, including smartphones, tablets and watches, had surpassed 1 million units since its launch. Xiaomi has sold about 150,000 smartphones based on the Xring O1 chip since its May 2025 launch, according to the sources. MEMORY COSTS PUSHING UP PRICES Smartphone makers are contending with a global downturn in device sales, as memory and component costs push up prices and squeeze demand. Xiaomi sold 65 million handsets in the first half of 2026 at an average price of 1,329 yuan ($197.74), compared with 84 million units sold at an average price of 1,141 yuan in the same period of 2025 and 83 million units at 1,123 yuan in 2024, according to data from Visible Alpha by S&P Global. Global smartphone shipments are expected to decline 14% in 2026, according to research firm International Data Corporation. Xiaomi said on Monday it had also contracted TSMC to manufacture two other Xring chips: the Xring O100, a 6-nm neural processing unit that will support Xiaomi's large language model, MiMo, on consumer electronic devices, and the Xring D100, a 3-nm chip for autonomous driving. According to Xiaomi, the O3 has already entered mass production, while the O100 and D100 have completed development and are slated for deployment next year.

item.title: Germany's Uniper signs 15-year gas import deal with Norway's Equinor
item.description: Germany's Uniper has signed a deal to import more than 30 terawatt hours of gas a year from Equinor from 2027, the companies said on Monday, reinforcing Norway's position as the key supplier to Europe's biggest economy.
item.dc:creator: Nora Buli, Christoph Steitz
item.content:encoded: Germany's Uniper (UN0k.DE) has signed a deal to import more than 30 terawatt hours of gas a year from Equinor (EQNR.OL) from 2027, the companies said on Monday, reinforcing Norway's position as the key supplier to Europe's biggest economy. The deal, equivalent to around 2.8 billion cubic metres of natural gas per year, runs until the end of 2041, and equates to nearly 3% of Germany's annual gas imports. Norway supplied 44% of Germany's gas imports, according to network regulator Bundesnetzagentur, taking Russia's place as the largest supplier after Moscow ended most energy ties with Europe following its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The contract with Equinor marks Uniper's latest effort to diversify its supplies and follows its [USN:L6N43U0J6 TEXT:"agreement"] with Canada as companies seek to bolster energy security after shortages linked to the Iran war. "For us it's really important that we rebuild our portfolio," Uniper CEO Michael Lewis told Reuters after signing the deal in Stavanger, Norway, adding the agreement could not come at a more important moment. "When you look at the turbulence in the energy markets over the last few years, it's critical that we diversify our energy supplies. Different suppliers, different routes, whether that's pipeline or LNG," Lewis said. LONG-TERM GAS DEMAND Both Lewis and Equinor CEO Anders Opedal stressed the importance of Norwegian supply for European energy security. The agreement also sends a strong signal from European industry that Norwegian gas will remain in demand for years to come, Opedal told Reuters. "This is the first contract that goes into the 2040s," he said. The companies also said they would expand cooperation on lower-emission gas projects, highlighting the relatively low carbon intensity of Norwegian gas, although they did not provide further details. Lewis said gas would remain a necessary transition fuel as Germany seeks to phase out coal, arguing that increased gas use in the near term could lower emissions while supporting longer-term decarbonisation goals in combination with carbon capture technology. Sources previously [USN:L1N42A0NN TEXT:"told"] Reuters that Equinor is among the parties interested in state-owned Uniper, which Berlin is seeking to divest after rescuing the utility during Europe's energy crisis in 2022. Opedal declined to comment when asked whether Equinor had expressed interest in the stake.

item.title: Shein fashions bizarre upside-down IPO
item.description: The online retailer is targeting a $27 bln valuation at best, almost 75% below its peak. Side deals mean it’ll pay some $3.5 bln, twice the IPO proceeds, to any invested at those higher levels. Professional risk-takers ought to wear their mistakes, not be compensated for them.
item.dc:creator: Katrina Hamlin
item.content:encoded: Shein’s IPO turns the concept of capital raising upside-down. The online retailer is now hoping to raise $1.8 billion in its looming stock market debut. But at the same time it will be paying around double that to investors in its private funding rounds since 2022 to make up for its shrunken valuation. In essence, that means these professional risk-takers are being compensated for their own mistakes. That's not how public listings are supposed to work. The problem stems from the near-75% decline in the value of Shein's equity, which stood at $98 billion in early 2022. Investors in a later round, where the company's worth had fallen to $64 billion, negotiated payouts in case it plummeted further. This March, the company extended the privilege to all who had sewn money into Shein at $60 billion or higher. That means the company now has to [USN:L4N44L004 TEXT:"stump up"] $3.5 billion in cash and another $120 million in stock to these irrationally exuberant venture capitalists. Sure, Shein has long insisted during its several attempts over the years to go public that it's not doing so because it needs the money. But it's bizarre indeed, to say the least, to push ahead with an IPO that costs the company twice what it's raising. Adding to the topsy-turvy nature of Shein's capital-raising saga, some of its current shareholders are coming back for more: Boyu Capital, General Atlantic and Tiger Global are among those to sign up as cornerstone investors for the offering, which will be Hong Kong’s largest this year. Given that Shein may yet deserve a deeper discount, they may be in for more pain. That's because even a $27 billion valuation looks punchy. Assume revenue hits $36 billion this year, based on annualising the adjusted first-quarter sales number. Assume 4.5% growth in 2027 and a net margin of around 3.5%, and Shein's net profit could hit $1.4 billion. Pop that on 20 times multiple, a tad below the 24.5 times Zara-owner Inditex (ITX.MC) sports, per Visible Alpha, and the equity would be worth what Shein wants IPO investors to pay for it. But the company is grappling with the end of import duty exemptions for low-value parcels in the U.S., new fees on such shipments in Europe, and investigations in both regions – which are its two largest markets. Sales grew only 1% in the first quarter, with a 2.5% net margin, after adjusting for one-off charges. And the 20 times multiple is overly generous: Inditex and other listed fashion peers have margins closer to 10%, as well as stronger sales growth. Sure, Shein could don a nattier performance than that, but it would take time to prove that any rapid recovery were sustainable. Its messy IPO is setting the scene for a financial fashion faux pas. Follow Katrina Hamlin on Bluesky and Linkedin . Online fashion retailer Shein Global will price its shares at up to HK$49.50 each according to a filing on August 24. At the upper end of the range, the company could raise HK$13.9 billion ($1.8 billion), implying a valuation of $26.8 billion. Shein will pay out as much as $2.2 billion in compensation to early investors, assuming the final offer price is at the low end of the range, and issue an additional 19.6 billion in stock, worth about $120 million. It is also paying out $1.3 billion in cash to holders of Series pre-D, D and D plus preferred shares, who bought in when the company was valued at $60 billion or more. Cornerstone investors led by existing shareholders Boyu, Tiger Global and General Atlantic have subscribed for about $383 million worth of Shein shares, the prospectus showed. Tencent, Greenwoods, Taikang Life and UBS Asset Management will also take stock. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Trump's Kim gambit deepens doubts over US reliability at a key moment for Asia
item.description: Donald Trump's olive branch to North Korea's Kim Jong Un at the expense of a long-standing ally comes at a pivotal moment for U.S. security ties in Asia, as partners from Japan to India reassess how much they can rely on Washington.
item.dc:creator: John Geddie, Yukiko Toyoda, Ben Blanchard, Aftab Ahmed
item.content:encoded: Donald Trump's olive branch to North Korea's Kim Jong Un at the expense of a long-standing ally comes at a pivotal moment for U.S. security ties in Asia, as partners from Japan to India reassess how much they can rely on Washington. The U.S. president's abrupt decision to [USN:L1N44D05G TEXT:"cut back"] military drills with South Korea last week, which he described as hostile to Pyongyang, has reinforced fears that Trump's unpredictability could strain alliances that have long maintained peace in the region, government officials and security experts said. Japan worries it too could find itself in Trump's cross-hairs as it embarks on thorny security negotiations; Taiwan is warily watching an upcoming summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping; and India is growing less certain of its place in Washington's strategic calculus. "The decision will certainly fuel growing doubts in the region about U.S. security commitments," said Jeremy Chan, a senior analyst with political risk consultancy Eurasia Group and former U.S. diplomat in Japan and China. Adding to the anxiety, the United States [USN:L6N44L07Y TEXT:"cancelled"] another military exercise with South Korea scheduled for next month, Seoul said on Monday, after Washington cited constraints on U.S. forces due to the Iran war. Trump has been frustrated by the failure of U.S. allies to support the war and made it clear that many of them must spend more on their own defence, a White House official said when asked about such concerns. He is [USN:L4N44H048 TEXT:"eager to restart talks"] with North Korea and secure a win on the international stage to counter his unpopular conflict with Iran, according to a person briefed on discussions between U.S. and South Korean officials. 'EXTREMELY TROUBLING' FOR TOKYO Trump's push to meet Kim - which has so far drawn a [USN:L4N44H048 TEXT:"frosty response"] from Pyongyang - could backfire and embolden nuclear-armed North Korea, said Itsunori Onodera, an influential Japanese lawmaker and former defence minister. Such a prospect is "extremely troubling" for Tokyo, he said on a Fuji TV news programme last Thursday. Despite Trump's overtures, Pyongyang [USN:L1N44H09Z TEXT:"fired a volley"] of ballistic missiles off its east coast earlier that day, triggering alerts in neighbouring South Korea and Japan. What worries Japanese officials more is Trump's approach as Tokyo embarks on talks with Washington over how much it should pay towards the cost of hosting U.S. forces, America's largest overseas deployment. Japan is bracing for the possibility that Trump could, with little warning, demand a sharp hike that would be politically difficult to swallow, said a senior Japanese government official, requesting anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter. Trump could also wield upcoming U.S. military exercises with Japan in October as leverage, analysts say. Officials in Washington and Tokyo said they did not expect the exercises to be curtailed, though Trump could change his mind at any point, they cautioned. The drills, known as Keen Sword, may already be smaller than their 2024 iteration because of the diversion of U.S. assets and personnel to the conflict with Iran. That shift - which recently saw America's only forward-deployed aircraft carrier in Asia, the USS George Washington, depart for the Middle East to relieve the beleaguered USS Abraham Lincoln - has stirred concern that U.S. deterrence against China [USN:L1N3ZR088 TEXT:"is being eroded"]. During a visit to Asia this month, Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby said working with allies to ensure combat readiness along the so-called first island chain that runs from Japan through the Philippines is a priority for Washington. TRUMP, XI AND TAIWAN Nowhere are concerns about China's growing military pressure more acute than in Taiwan, the democratically governed island claimed by Beijing. Trump has held up approval of a $14 billion package of arms sales to Taipei in order to maintain warm relations and a fragile trade truce with China's Xi. As Trump prepares for his latest round of summitry with Xi in Washington next month, officials in Taipei say they expect Washington will at the very least carve up the arms sales into smaller chunks to try and avoid upsetting Beijing too much. Domingo Yang of the Taiwan defence ministry's think tank, the Institute for National Defence and Security Research, says there is a distinction between Trump's rhetoric and actual U.S. behaviour, noting U.S. intelligence sharing, training and patrols with Taiwan remain substantial. A U.S. Navy aircraft [USN:L1N44J00A TEXT:"transited the Taiwan Strait"] on Friday in a move the United States described as demonstrating its "commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific." Trump's latest actions have also rocked confidence in India, where the U.S. risks squandering years of efforts to draw New Delhi closer as a counterweight to Russia and China, security analysts say. It also comes after the Pentagon's decision in June to rename its Asia military headquarters to Pacific Command from Indo-Pacific Command, a move some analysts say is a sign India is no longer as strategically important to Washington. The Pentagon denied any such shift. But Trump's steep tariffs on Indian exports and repeated claims that he had mediated an India-Pakistan ceasefire had already exasperated New Delhi. Officials there are now "very, very cautious" about committing to long-term defence deals with Washington, according to two Indian sources with knowledge of the matter. "The latest decision only reinforces President Trump's transactional view of foreign affairs and serves as a reminder that differences over specific policies, even among allies, can carry costs for the broader bilateral relationship," said Pearl Pandya, senior analyst at Armed Conflict Location & Event Data, a conflict monitoring group.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS L'Europe indécise avant une semaine chargée, focus sur le Moyen-Orient et Nvidia (actualisé)
item.description: Les principales Bourses européennes sont attendues sur une note hésitante lundi à l'ouverture, les investisseurs faisant preuve de prudence en ce début de semaine riche en événements géopolitiques et en données macroéconomiques, sans parler des résultats attendus du géant des puces électroniques Nvidia et du symposium de Jackson Hole.
item.dc:creator: Diana Mandia
item.content:encoded: Les principales Bourses européennes sont attendues sur une note hésitante lundi à l'ouverture, les investisseurs faisant preuve de prudence en ce début de semaine riche en événements géopolitiques et en données macroéconomiques, sans parler des résultats attendus du géant des puces électroniques Nvidia et du symposium de Jackson Hole. Les contrats à terme sur indices suggèrent une ouverture baisse de 0,07% pour le CAC 40 parisien (.FCHI) et de 0,16% pour le Dax à Francfort (.GDAXI) . Le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) est attendu stable et le FTSE de la Bourse de Londres pourrait prendre 0,15%. La confiance des investisseurs devrait rester modérée ce lundi, les négociations de paix au Moyen-Orient demeurant dans l'impasse, ce qui met les marchés pétroliers sous tension et a entraîné une hausse de 5% des prix du pétrole au cours de la semaine dernière. La retenue s'impose d'autant plus dans le contexte d'une nouvelle escalade verbale entre les États-Unis et l'Iran. Washington a fait part vendredi de son intention d'infliger à la République islamique "les plus sévères sanctions de son histoire", selon les termes du secrétaire au Trésor Scott Bessent, qui doit détailler ces mesures lundi à 14h00 heure de Washington (18h00 GMT). "On ne sait pas encore si la politique américaine visant à isoler économiquement l'Iran s'avérera efficace", écrit dans une note Vivek Dhar, analyste spécialisé dans les matières premières à la Commonwealth Bank of Australia. "Mais si les mesures américaines produisent les effets escomptés, la capacité de l'Iran à riposter par une escalade de la violence deviendra un risque croissant dont les marchés de l'énergie devront tenir compte". Le chef de l'armée pakistanaise, Asim Munir, [USN:L8N44K01M TEXT:"se rendra"] lundi à Téhéran dans le cadre des efforts de médiation d'Islamabad dans le conflit entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran, a déclaré dimanche le porte-parole du ministère iranien des Affaires étrangères. Le ministre des Affaires étrangères d'Oman se rendra pour sa part mardi à Téhéran afin de poursuivre ses discussions avec l'Iran concernant le détroit d'Ormuz, selon le porte-parole du ministère. Les négociations entre Oman et l'Iran sur Ormuz ont déjà suscité la colère des États-Unis ces dernières semaines. Les opérateurs espèrent également obtenir des éclaircissements sur les perspectives des taux d'intérêt américains ou sur les turbulences du marché obligataire lorsque le président de la Réserve fédérale (Fed), Kevin Warsh, prendra la parole vendredi à Jackson Hole, dans le Wyoming, même si sa réticence à donner des indications prospectives laisse craindre des déclarations plutôt prudentes. Les chiffres de l'inflation PCE aux États-Unis, l'indicateur privilégié par la Fed pour fixer ses taux, seront aussi publiés cette semaine et pourraient encore influencer les anticipations du marché concernant la réunion de septembre, qui estiment à 40% la probabilité d'une hausse des coûts d'emprunt. Les marchés observeront également avec attention la publication des résultats trimestriels de plusieurs géants de la tech, notamment ceux de Nvidia (NVDA.O) mercredi. "Ces dernières années, les résultats financiers de Nvidia ont souvent constitué à eux seuls un événement macroéconomique majeur, suscitant des réactions comparables à celles provoquées par les rapports sur l'emploi aux États-Unis et les chiffres de l'IPC", écrivent les analystes de Deutsche Bank. "Cependant, au cours des derniers trimestres, les surprises positives en matière de résultats n'ont pas été aussi importantes que celles observées en 2023-2024, et à l'issue de chacune des quatre dernières publications de résultats, le cours de l'action Nvidia a en réalité baissé le lendemain", ajoutent-ils. LES VALEURS A SUIVRE : [USN:L8N44I0XK] A WALL STREET La Bourse de New York a fini dans le vert vendredi mais enregistre des pertes hebdomadaires, les turbulences sur le marché obligataire et les tensions géopolitiques freinant l'appétit pour le risque. L'indice Dow Jones (.DJI) a gagné 0,98%, le Standard & Poor's 500 (.SPX) , plus large, a pris 0,43%, et le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) a avancé de son côté de 0,44%. EN ASIE L'indice Nikkei (.N225) de la Bourse de Tokyo a perdu 0,74%, affecté par la prudence entourant les valeurs liées à l'intelligence artificielle (IA) avant les résultats de Nvidia. Le marché japonais est également pénalisé par les craintes liées à l'inflation : les investisseurs et analystes s'attendent à ce que la Banque du Japon (BoJ) relève ses taux d'intérêt le mois prochain lors de sa prochaine réunion de politique monétaire. Le Kospi (.KS11) a reculé de 3,12%, Samsung (005930.KS) abandonnant 8,7%. Les investisseurs se montrent déçus par le plan de redistribution aux actionnaires annoncé par le géant des puces, car ils espéraient notamment bénéficier d'une part plus importante des excédents de trésorerie générés par l'IA. En Chine, l'indice composite de la Bourse de Shanghai (.SSEC) perd 0,96% et le CSI 300 (.CSI300) des grandes capitalisations abandonne 1,59%, pénalisés par une émission surprise d'actions d'Alibaba (9988.HK) (-9,27%) avec une décote de 8,4% par rapport à son cours de clôture de vendredi. Il s'agit de la plus importante offre publique secondaire jamais réalisée à Hong Kong, destinée à financer les projets de développement du géant du commerce en ligne dans le domaine de l'IA . "L'ADN d'Alibaba réside dans le commerce électronique, et non dans les technologies de pointe", déclare Yang Tingwu, directeur général adjoint de la société de gestion d'actifs Tongheng Investment. "Peu importe le montant qu'elle investisse dans le matériel d'IA, elle risque fort d'être devancée par ses concurrents en matière d'innovation technologique", ajoute-t-il. La Bourse de Hong Kong (.HSI) cède 2,08%. Le groupe de "fast fashion" Shein a par ailleurs [USN:L6N44L01T TEXT:"confirmé"] lundi son intention d'entrer en Bourse à Hong Kong le 1er septembre. TAUX / CHANGES Les rendements obligataires sont en légère baisse lundi, même si le plan du Trésor américain visant à doubler le montant de ses rachats de dette à long terme n'a pas eu d'effets significatifs, dans un contexte de hausse générale des coûts de financement des principales économies mondiales. Le rendement des Treasuries à dix ans perd 3,2 points de base à 4,7060%. Le deux ans recule de près de 1 point de base à 4,2252%. Dans la zone euro, le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans cède 1,5 point de base à 3,2415%. Le deux ans est également en légère baisse et ressort à 2,8232%. Sur le marché des changes, le dollar grappille 0,06% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) , tout en se situant près de ses plus bas niveaux de ces derniers mois, sur un marché déstabilisé par la promesse du Trésor américain de racheter davantage d'obligations. L'euro est quasi stable (-0,03%) à 1,1676 dollar . PÉTROLE Les cours du pétrole reculent lundi, les investisseurs prenant leurs bénéfices avant des détails sur les nouvelles sanctions américains contre l'Iran, susceptibles de perturber davantage l'approvisionnement en provenance du Moyen-Orient. Le Brent perd 1,63% à 92,85 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) 1,99% à 85,33 dollars. AUCUN INDICATEUR ÉCONOMIQUE MAJEUR À L'AGENDA DU 24 AOÛT

item.title: Coach carrying German high-school students crashes in Netherlands
item.description: A coach carrying high-school students from Germany crashed in the east of the Netherlands early on Monday, injuring eight people, who were taken to hospital, Dutch police said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
